title: Diagonal Matrix Game Value
body_html:
Diagonal Matrix Game Value

Let $A$ be the diagonal $n\times n$ matrix with diagonal entries $a_i>0$. Then $$ \operatorname{val}(A)= \left(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^{-1}\right)^{-1}. $$ Both players have the same optimal mixed strategy $p\in\Delta(\{1,\ldots,n\})$ given by $$ p_i= \frac{a_i^{-1}}{\sum_{k=1}^n a_k^{-1}}. $$
proof_html:
Let $$ c=\left(\sum_{k=1}^n a_k^{-1}\right)^{-1} \quad\text{and}\quad p_i=ca_i^{-1}. $$ Then $p$ is a probability vector. Against any pure column $j$, the row player's payoff from $p$ is $p_ja_j=c$, so $p$ guarantees $c$. Against any pure row $i$, the column player's mixed strategy $p$ gives payoff $a_ip_i=c$, so $p$ holds the row player to $c$. By weak duality, the value is $c$ and $p$ is optimal for both players.

References

  • [MFoGT, Section 2.8, Exercise 6] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory. Compute value and optimal strategies for a positive diagonal matrix game.
